tickets.title: Churned Shoppers (LEFT JOIN)
tickets.description: Performs a LEFT JOIN to find all customers who signed up but have never placed an order.
tasks: Performs a LEFT JOIN to find all customers who signed up but have never placed an order.
learning_objectives: Master relational data retrieval across multiple tables.
tickets.evaluation: `compare_result_set(actual, expected)` `check_command_used("LEFT JOIN")` `check_document_count(actual, expected_churned)` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts for correct listing; 10 pts if INNER JOIN used instead (yielding empty result). **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts if index on `customer_id` is matched. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for explicit alias definitions (`c` and `o`).
common_mistakes: Using a CROSS JOIN accidentally by forgetting the ON clause.
Selecting ambiguous column names without table aliases.
hints: Ensure you are joining on the correct primary and foreign keys.
Consider whether an INNER JOIN or LEFT JOIN is needed.

solution.query.sql:
SELECT c.id AS customer_id, c.name, c.email
    FROM customers c
    LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
    WHERE o.id IS NULL
    ORDER BY c.name ASC;

tickets.title: Category Sales Performance (Three-Way JOIN)
tickets.description: Joins the tables to calculate the total quantity sold and total revenue per product category.
tasks: Joins the tables to calculate the total quantity sold and total revenue per product category.
learning_objectives: Master relational data retrieval across multiple tables.
tickets.evaluation: `compare_result_set(actual, expected)` `check_command_used("JOIN")` `check_sort_order(actual, 'total_revenue', 'DESC')` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts for category match and sums. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts for join order execution. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for explicit column calculations.
common_mistakes: Using a CROSS JOIN accidentally by forgetting the ON clause.
Selecting ambiguous column names without table aliases.
hints: Ensure you are joining on the correct primary and foreign keys.
Consider whether an INNER JOIN or LEFT JOIN is needed.

solution.query.sql:
SELECT
      p.category,
      SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity,
      SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price_per_unit) AS total_revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id
    GROUP BY p.category
    ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

tickets.title: Product Recommendations (Self JOIN)
tickets.description: Pairs distinct products in the same category that are within $15 price difference for shopping suggestions.
tasks: Pairs distinct products in the same category that are within $15 price difference for shopping suggestions.
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and querying.
tickets.evaluation: `compare_result_set(actual, expected)` `check_command_used("ABS")` `check_join_condition(p1.id < p2.id to prevent duplication)` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts for correct product pairings. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts if pricing ranges leverage table indices. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for removing self-pairing mirror records.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without backticks.
hints: Review the MySQL documentation for exact syntax.
Test your queries in smaller chunks first.

solution.query.sql:
SELECT p1.name AS prod_a, p2.name AS prod_b, p1.category, ABS(p1.price - p2.price) AS price_diff
    FROM products p1
    JOIN products p2 ON p1.category = p2.category AND p1.id < p2.id
    WHERE ABS(p1.price - p2.price) <= 15.00
    ORDER BY price_diff ASC;
